changes.comment: ai-assist: (1) executeClientToolTurn refuses a caller-built resolvedThinking whose OpenAI-format effort (openAiEffort, or xaiEffort) is 'none' when the model is on thinkingRequiredModelPrefixes (gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra, grok-4.7/4.6/4.5), before the wire, with '<model> cannot run with thinking off: set openAiEffort to an effort other than 'none'' — the provider 400s it; anthropicThinkingDisabled already had the same guard. (2) New IAiProviderDescriptor.chatOutputTokensField ('max_tokens' | 'max_completion_tokens', exported type ChatOutputTokensField) declares the Chat Completions output-token field; usesMaxCompletionTokensField now reads it instead of matching the provider id 'openai'. OpenAI, Groq and xAI Grok declare 'max_completion_tokens' (each API reference marks max_tokens deprecated), so Groq and xAI chat requests now send maxTokens as max_completion_tokens rather than max_tokens; Mistral, Ollama and openai-compat keep max_tokens. A hand-built descriptor that relied on id 'openai' to get max_completion_tokens must now declare the field. (3) resolveProviderModel — and the completion, streaming, client-tool and resolveMaxOutputTokens paths through it — fails with the provider id and the offending key's path on a ModelSpec outside its type (e.g. { base: undefined } from untyped JSON) instead of throwing a TypeError; resolveModel resolves such a spec to ''.
